Reading AIS Data: What Vessel Trackers Actually Show

By Hormuz Watch Editorial · 6 September 2026 · 7 min read

The Automatic Identification System (AIS) was designed for collision avoidance, not for public intelligence dashboards — but its open broadcasts make it the backbone of commercial vessel tracking.

Each broadcast includes the vessel's MMSI identity, position, speed over ground, course, and a manually entered destination — that last field is typed by the crew and is frequently outdated or aspirational, so treat it with scepticism.

Gaps in coverage are normal: terrestrial receivers have limited range, and satellite AIS has revisit delays. A vessel "disappearing" from a tracker usually means a coverage gap, not an incident.

Note: the vessel markers on this site are fictional demonstration data, not real AIS positions.
